title: Runtime Skew Workaround (Standard Toolchain Pinning)
pattern: Hardcoding target-skew, pointer-width, or compiler-version compatibility fallbacks in core, transitively-shared libraries to appease a tiny handful of legacy clients who refuse to upgrade their runtimes.
why_bad: System-wide stagnation. Tying core, fleet-wide shared libraries to legacy runtime constraints blocks performance optimizations, delays standard compiler upgrades, and spreads target-specific complexity to completely unrelated systems.
detection:
The linter must observe:
1. Low-level platform checks (e.g., pointer-width, archaic target OS flags) embedded in high-level business logic.
2. The check exists solely to accommodate a specific, outdated deployment target.
counterexample:
`Context-dependent`
```rust
// Valid: Legitimate multi-platform support in a hardware-abstracting library
```
source: - Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google* (2020) [348]
